chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ibn Miskan from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man married a woman, then went to a land and married her sister, without knowing. He said: 'He may keep whichever he wishes and release the other.'

Thus this report is not contradictory to what we have mentioned before, because his saying (peace be upon him) 'he may keep whichever he wishes' is understood to mean: if he wishes to keep the first, he keeps her with a firm, established contract; and if he wishes to keep the second, he divorces the first and then keeps the second with a new contract. So there is no contradiction between the reports. And whenever a man divorces his wife with a revocable divorce, it is not permissible for him to contract marriage with her sister. And whenever he divorces her with an irrevocable divorce, or she dies, or separation occurs by one of the forms of irrevocable separation, there is no harm upon him in contracting marriage with her sister immediately.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marrying two sisters in Shia jurisprudence according to the hadith of Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the juristic nuance of marrying two sisters by distinguishing between simultaneous possession and sequential contracting. The commentary explains that 'keeping' either sister requires either maintaining the first with a firm contract or divorcing her to initiate a new contract with the second, thereby avoiding the prohibition of *al-jam'* (simultaneous marriage). It further refines the conditions under which the second sister becomes permissible, specifically noting that a revocable divorce (*raj'i*) does not permit immediate marriage to the sister, whereas an irrevocable separation (*baynunah*) does.
